editorialBrief.readerQuestion: Where do the Rowdies play, and what makes their ground worth knowing?
editorialBrief.usefulOutcome: Find Al Lang in downtown St. Petersburg and learn its baseball-to-soccer history.
editorialBrief.copyDirection: Specific local detail, short sentences and one honest question.

caption:
The Tampa Bay Rowdies play across the bay, right on the waterfront in downtown St. Petersburg.

Al Lang was a baseball ground before the Rowdies made it home in 2011. Their first match there was on April 9, a 1–0 win over Montreal.

If you’ve been to Al Lang, which section would you recommend to someone going for the first time?

caption:
Two teams to follow in downtown Orlando: City in MLS and Pride in the NWSL. Both play at Inter.co Stadium in downtown Orlando.

The ground opened in March 2017. If it’s been a while since your last match, you may remember it under an earlier name.

City, Pride, or both? And what’s your pre-match stop nearby?

editorialBrief.audience: Players and parents in western Broward comparing clubs
editorialBrief.readerQuestion: What can I find at Weston FC, and what should I ask before an evaluation?
editorialBrief.usefulOutcome: Find the official boys and girls program pages and ask about age groups, team level and training venue.
editorialBrief.copyDirection: Club-specific photography, concise questions, no invented opening or roster offer.

caption:
Looking at Weston FC? Start with the program pages, then ask about the team for your age group.

The club has boys’ and girls’ programs. Its boys’ page lists MLS NEXT, UPSL and other leagues; that doesn’t mean every team plays at the same level or has spaces available.

Before an evaluation, ask which team you’re being considered for, where it trains and what the season costs. Those answers matter more than a league badge on its own.

Boys: https://www.westonfc.org/about-1-1
Girls: https://www.westonfc.org/about-1-2
